metadata.description: Environment short name (staging | prod).
Azure region. Singapore for PDPA.
App Service Plan SKU.
Postgres SKU.
Postgres server resource name. Leave empty for inspro-<env>-pg; production can override this after a PITR cutover without recreating the recovered server.
Postgres tier.
Postgres admin username.
Bootstrap-only Postgres admin password. Leave empty for every routine deployment so the database credential is never rewritten.
Postgres backup retention days. Prod overrides to 35.

Enable geo-redundant Postgres backups. NOTE: the paired region for southeastasia is East Asia (Hong Kong), so enabling this copies member/claims data OUT of Singapore. Leave false unless that has been signed off against PDPA.
Postgres data disk size. IOPS is derived from it, NOT from the compute SKU: 32GiB=120, 64GiB=240, 128GiB=500, 256GiB=1100. 32GiB is the throughput floor.
Enable zone-redundant Postgres HA. Not supported on the Burstable tier, and roughly doubles cost (a standby duplicates compute+storage).
Azure Managed Redis SKU, for example Balanced_B0.

Provision Redis at all. Both consumers degrade gracefully without it — the AI response cache falls back to in-memory and SlowAPI to per-process counters (see app/services/ai_cache.py and app/core/rate_limit.py) — so non-prod can skip the cost. Prod keeps it: per-process rate-limit counters would multiply every limit by the worker count.
Entra tenant ID.
Entra client ID for the API app registration.
CORS origins (comma-separated). In prod every entry must be an https origin; the app refuses to start on a wildcard, plaintext or localhost entry.

Public https origin of the portal, used for links in outbound mail (INSPRO_FRONTEND_ORIGIN), e.g. https://portal.example.com. Leave empty for the web app's default host, https://<siteName>.azurewebsites.net. In prod the app refuses to start on a missing, non-https or localhost origin.
Exact trusted reverse-proxy peers for Uvicorn. Never use a wildcard on a public listener.
Fully-qualified container image, e.g. insproacr.azurecr.io/inspro-api:<sha>. The CI must build+push the image before passing this in.
Signing secret for employee-portal member JWTs (min 32 chars). The app refuses to boot in prod without one — generate with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"

Fernet master key that decrypts per-tenant BYOK AI keys (client_ai_configs). Vertex/Gemini BYOK is the sole AI path in prod, so without this every decrypt fails and AI silently falls closed. Generate with: python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
One-time initialization switch for a brand-new environment. Routine and drift deployments must leave this false; it is not a rotation mechanism.
ACR registry hostname for the webapp to pull from, e.g. insproacr.azurecr.io.
Resource group holding the container registry.
Web app / hostname. Defaults to inspro-<env>-api; prod uses inspro-portal so the public URL is inspro-portal.azurewebsites.net.
Apex domain for tenant-per-subdomain routing. Empty on single-host deployments (no custom domain).
How HR/portal requests name their tenant. "subdomain" needs wildcard DNS + a wildcard cert; "header" is for a single shared hostname.
Gunicorn worker processes. Keep at or below the plan vCPU count — it also divides the AI concurrency limit and multiplies the DB pool.
SQLAlchemy pool size PER WORKER. Ceiling is workers x (pool + overflow) x instances; keep it under the server max_connections.
SQLAlchemy overflow connections per worker.
Concurrent durable claim reviews in the dedicated worker process.
Hard concurrent claim-review cap per company. Must not exceed reviewWorkerConcurrency.
SQLAlchemy pool size for the dedicated claim-review worker process.
SQLAlchemy overflow connections for the dedicated claim-review worker process.

Integrate the web app with the VNet so it reaches Postgres over the private endpoint. Setting this to false stops NEW deployments wiring the subnet, but does not tear down existing integration — for a rollback run `az webapp vnet-integration remove` as well, which reverts the app to the public path.
Hosts that serve the platform owner's firm and the master-admin console (INSPRO_PLATFORM_HOSTS, comma-separated, no scheme). Leave empty to keep the app default: the INSPRO_FRONTEND_ORIGIN host.

Run the web app and worker as the least-privilege database login (Key Vault secret database-url-app, role inspro_app: no DDL) and leave new firm schemas to the migration job (INSPRO_RUNTIME_PROVISIONING=false). Turn on only after docs/DATABASE_ROLES_RUNBOOK.md has been applied and verified; off keeps the current connection.
Provision Front Door Premium (profile, endpoint, WAF, rule set, routes, customer domains) in front of the web app. Off: no Front Door resource exists and the site is unchanged.

Set INSPRO_FRONT_DOOR_ID on the web app. The app then refuses requests without this profile's X-Azure-FDID (except /health and /readiness) and takes the public host from X-Inspro-Edge-Host. Turn on only after the edge hostname has been verified.

Lock the web app's main site to this Front Door profile: allow service tag AzureFrontDoor.Backend with X-Azure-FDID equal to the profile ID, deny everything else. The SCM site keeps its own (open) rules. Turn on last.

WAF mode. Detection (default) logs rule matches without blocking, for the first rollout while false positives on uploads and JSON bodies are tuned out; switch to Prevention once the WAF logs are clean.

Hostnames served through Front Door, each with the firm that owns it: [{ "hostname": "benefits.acme.com", "firmSlug": "acme" }]. Each gets a Front Door-managed certificate (TLS 1.2 minimum) and is bound to the routes and the WAF. Onboard with infra/scripts/onboard_domain.py.
Primary notification email for production alerts (optional).
Additional notification emails. Production declares its named responders here to avoid duplicate delivery through forwarding aliases.

Log Analytics retention in days. 90 meets the 90-day security/audit log requirement in docs/PRODUCTION_RESILIENCE_RUNBOOK.md. Retention beyond the free period (31 days for most tables) is billed per GB-month of retained data, which at this volume is small next to ingestion.

Log Analytics daily ingestion cap in GB (-1 = no cap). A cost backstop against a runaway log loop: 2 GB/day bounds ingestion at roughly 60 GB a month. Once the cap is reached, ingestion stops until the daily reset, so the rest of that day's logs, Application Insights telemetry and log-based alerts are lost. Keep it well above normal daily volume (see the Usage table).
Portal mail delivery mode. Keep disabled until a verified STARTTLS SMTP sender is configured.
SMTP host for portal OTP and claim-update mail.
SMTP port.
SMTP username (also the default From address).
From address for portal OTP mail (defaults to smtpUser).
Bootstrap-only SMTP password. Routine deployments leave this empty.

properties.Description: Checks that the production web process is externally reachable from Singapore.

properties.Description: Checks the production portal, PostgreSQL, and Redis path from Singapore.

properties.description: The production website is not reachable from the Singapore availability probe.
A production dependency is unavailable from the Singapore readiness probe.
An Azure resource in the Singapore production resource group became degraded or unavailable.
The oldest available claim-review job exceeded the configured queue-age threshold.
A lease, provider, terminal-job, or state-invariant failure requires attention.

allOf.query:
traces
            | extend code = tostring(customDimensions.error_code)
            | where code == "lease_expired"
                or code startswith "ai_configuration"
                or code in ("pending_without_job", "active_missing_record")
                or message == "Claim-review job terminated"

metadata.description: Resource name prefix, e.g. inspro-prod.
Azure region. Must match the app and the database — regional VNet integration requires all three in the same region.
Existing Postgres Flexible Server to place behind a private endpoint.
Private endpoint resource name for the selected PostgreSQL server. A PITR cutover uses a new endpoint so the source endpoint remains available for rollback.
VNet address space. 10.0.0.0/16 and 10.1.0.0/16 are already taken by rg-ivm and rg-supabase-sea in this subscription.
Subnet delegated to App Service for regional VNet integration. Microsoft recommends at least a /26 — App Service consumes addresses per instance during scale and slot swaps.
Subnet holding the Postgres private endpoint NIC.
Subnet the web app integrates with. Consumed by main.bicep as virtualNetworkSubnetId.
Resource name prefix, e.g. inspro-prod.
The App Service default hostname Front Door forwards to, e.g. inspro-portal.azurewebsites.net.
WAF mode. Detection logs matches without blocking; Prevention blocks requests whose anomaly score reaches the threshold.

Hostnames to serve, as [{ hostname, firmSlug }]: hostname is fully qualified (prefer a subdomain; an apex cannot take a CNAME), firmSlug is the owning firm's broker_firms.slug and prefixes the resource name. Each needs a CNAME to the endpoint hostname and a _dnsauth TXT record before its certificate is issued.
Log Analytics workspace that receives the WAF log and Front Door metrics.
The profile's Front Door ID, sent to the origin as X-Azure-FDID.
The endpoint hostname brokers point their CNAME records at.
Name of the container registry in THIS resource group.
Principal ID of the managed identity that needs pull access.
Stable discriminator so multiple apps can each hold a grant.
Name of the container registry in THIS resource group.
Principal ID of the managed identity that needs pull access.
Stable discriminator so multiple apps can each hold a grant.
